title: OCI Image Index
description: Immutable, package-local CAS object at /p/<namespace>/<package>/o/sha256/<hex>.json: the bytes a registry served for an OCI image index, stored verbatim, where <hex> is sha256 of those bytes and is therefore the registry's own manifest digest. Deliberately open at every level — this index does not author these bytes, so subject, artifactType, annotations, urls, data and future image-spec fields must all validate. It constrains only the grammar the resolver depends on: schemaVersion, manifests[], each descriptor's mediaType/digest/size, and — on a descriptor that carries a platform object at all — that object's architecture and os, both of which the image-spec marks REQUIRED and the platform projection reads unconditionally. A descriptor may omit platform entirely; it may not carry a half-populated one.

schemaVersion.description: OCI image-spec image-index.md: REQUIRED, and for this version of the specification MUST be 2.

mediaType.description: application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json for an OCI index; registries also serve Docker manifest lists (application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.list.v2+json) in the same shape. Deliberately not constrained to a value: both implementations discriminate an index from a manifest on the presence of manifests[] alone, and a schema stricter than the code it gates would reject bytes the bot accepts.

manifests.description: The descriptors the resolver selects a platform from. Presence of this property is the discriminator that makes these bytes an image index rather than an image manifest — an image manifest carries config/layers instead and is refused, never stored. The array type is load-bearing, not decoration: `items` applies only to arrays in 2020-12, so an object-valued manifests would bypass every descriptor constraint below.

descriptor.description: OCI content descriptor (image-spec descriptor.md). mediaType, digest and size are REQUIRED there and are the three fields every registry emits. Open on everything else: annotations, urls, data and artifactType all occur in registry-served indices.

digest.description: The OCI digest grammar (image-spec descriptor.md), verbatim and algorithm-agnostic. Deliberately not narrowed to sha256: these are the registry's own digests for leaf manifests, not digests this index mints.

platform.description: OCI platform object. Absent entirely on attestation and referrer descriptors, and os == "unknown" is the attestation convention; both forms are valid here and are filtered downstream by core/render.py's platform projection, never rejected at this layer. Field names with a literal dot (os.version, os.features) match the OCI spec's own property names, not a nested os object. Open like every other level: unrecognised keys validate, so a future image-spec platform field needs no schema change here.
